# Design Document

## Overview

One module, `src/diagrams/databricks/`, serving three MIME types from one engine — the C4 precedent applied to Databricks' own configuration files. The design's center of gravity is reuse: shared-extension registration and `body:` routing already exist, the centralized canvas pieces (`connections/`, `elements/`, selection, context-menu and keyboard plumbing) already exist, the CST-and-splice writer discipline and the command/undo path already exist. Two things are genuinely designed here rather than consumed: the **core `layout:` block in the `.adp`** (Requirement 7, this spec's one core change), and the **client-side simulation path** for the mocked domain actions (Requirement 8) that keeps pretend-runs off the command bus entirely.

## Steering Document Alignment

### Technical Standards (tech.md)

- **Diagram storage** — the three body formats belong to Databricks' tooling and round-trip byte-identically; authored positions go to the `.adp` per the layout rule this spec added to tech.md.
- **Commands** — every real edit (task add/remove/rename/connect, property writes, repositions, the pause/continuous/development toggles) is an `ICommand` with an inverse. Simulated actions never touch the command bus (design decision below).
- **gRPC call shapes** — no new services and no new streams; elements travel as the existing `Element`/`Delta` with an `Any` payload per type, actions and properties ride the existing context channel.
- **Specifying a diagram type** — the five build steps (model, persistence, wire, client UI, remaining logic) order the tasks document.

### Project Structure (structure.md)

- `src/diagrams/databricks/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.Databricks/` (+ `.Tests`), `src/diagrams/databricks/client/`, `src/diagrams/databricks/api/databricks.proto`, `src/diagrams/databricks/examples/` — the layout every sibling module has. The module depends on core; core's only growth is the layout block, defined in core because the `.adp` format is core's.

## Code Reuse Analysis

### Existing Components to Leverage

- **`DiagramDefinition` with `SharedExtension: true` and `Icon`** — three definitions in one `Diagram.cs` (`Bundle`, `Job`, `Pipeline`), `.yml`/`.yaml`/`.json` never claimed on sight; icons `mdi-package-variant-closed`, `mdi-transit-connection-horizontal`, `mdi-pipe`.
- **`DiagramFilePair`** — `body:` resolution against the `.adp`'s own folder, and the `view:`-style header scanning that the new `resource:` header joins.
- **The Add flow** (`AddDiagramContextActionProvider`, `DiagramOptionTree`) — registration on a file with type suggestions (Requirement 1.2 implemented as suggestion logic in the module's `IDiagramDocumentFactory` metadata, surfaced through the existing choice dialog).
- **Central canvas library** (`src/client/src/canvas/`) — `BoxElement` for tasks/resources/libraries, `FrameElement` for target frames, `FixedBezierConnection` for DAG edges, `StraightConnection` for reference/override edges, `elementSelectionOf`/`useElementContextMenu`/`structuralShortcutFor` for all interaction plumbing.
- **The timeline's writer discipline** — line-CST parse, smallest-splice writes, byte-identity tests; and its stateless `rel:` relation-gesture and `new:` placement-id mechanisms for the job DAG's connect and toolbox drops.
- **The problems panel** (`IDiagramValidator` integration) for Requirement 12, following the azure-pipeline validator's shape.
- **`ExampleRegistrationTests`** — the shipped examples of Requirement 13 join the existing integration sweep that proves every example registration resolves and validates.

### Integration Points

- **Hierarchy/routing** — registrations route through the existing shared-extension path; nested `resources/*.yml` files inside a bundle register individually.
- **Context channel** — one resolver, one action provider, one property provider and one toolbox provider for the family, each switching on the target's MIME type, registered like every other module's.
- **History** — module commands dispatch through `IHistoryStackStore`; the new core `SetRegistrationLayoutCommand` rides the same stacks.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    ADP[.adp: mime + body + resource + layout] --> ROUTE[DiagramFileRouter]
    YML[databricks.yml / job .yml / pipeline .json] --> STORE[DatabricksDocumentStore line-CST]
    ROUTE --> SESS[Three session factories, one engine]
    STORE --> SESS
    SESS -->|Element + Any payload| CANVAS[Bundle / Job / Pipeline canvases]
    CANVAS -->|ExecuteAction, SetProperty| PROV[Context providers]
    PROV -->|ICommand + inverse| STORE
    CANVAS -->|reposition| LAYOUT[core layout: block in .adp]
    CANVAS -.->|simulated runs, client-only| CANVAS
```

## Components and Interfaces

### Backend: documents and models

- **`DatabricksDocumentStore`** — owns loading, parsing and saving all three body formats. YAML and JSON alike are held as a line CST (the raw lines plus a parsed model carrying line ranges), so every write is a splice and an untouched file saves byte-identically. Unknown constructs parse into `UnknownNode` entries that render as generic boxes and that no writer ever touches (Requirement 2.4).
- **Models** — `BundleModel` (bundle info, includes, variables, `Resource[]` with kind/key/defining file, `Target[]` with mode/default/overrides), `JobModel` (`JobTask[]` with key, type, dependsOn (+outcome), runIf, cluster binding; `JobCluster[]`; trigger/schedule/continuous), `PipelineModel` (name and scalars, `Library[]`, cluster summary, notifications). Each model element carries its source line range for splicing and diagnostics.
- **Writers** — `BundleWriter`, `JobWriter`, `PipelineWriter`: named splice operations only (insert task block, remove task block with its dependsOn references, rewrite a scalar, insert/remove a library entry, rewrite a task key plus every reference in the same command). A write that would violate the published schema shape is refused before any splice (Requirement 6.4).

### Backend: sessions and layout

- **Session factories** — one per MIME type over the shared store, mirroring `C4SessionFactory`: parse, project to `Element`s with the type's `Any` payload, compute layout, then overlay stored positions.
- **Computed layout** — job: longest-path layering left-to-right on the dependsOn DAG (cycle-tolerant: back-edges excluded from layering, still drawn); bundle: three bands (bundle / resources / target frames); pipeline: sources → pipeline → target with satellites beneath. All pure functions in the module, unit-tested on fixtures.
- **`RegistrationLayout` (core)** — reads and writes the `layout:` block: after the header lines, `layout:` followed by indented `<element-id>: <x> <y>` entries. Read merges over computed positions element-by-element; stale ids are ignored on read and dropped on the next write (Requirement 7.4/7.5). Lives beside `DiagramFilePair`; the `.adp` is ADP's own file, so the writer may normalize the block freely.
- **`SetRegistrationLayoutCommand` (core)** — one element's position write with the previous entry (or its absence) as the inverse; the module's move path dispatches it, so a reposition is one undo like everything else.

### Backend: context providers

- **`DatabricksContextSourceResolver`** — resolves element ids within a file level; understands the timeline's `new:{x},{y}` placement ids and `rel:{from}->{to}` gesture ids for the job type.
- **`DatabricksContextActionProvider`** — discovery and execution per Requirement 11: task menu (rename, set run-if, assign cluster, disconnect submenu, remove), canvas menu (add task by type, pause/resume), bundle and pipeline menus, plus the simulated entries which discover with their marker but execute as a no-op `Completed` (the client plays the show — see below). Rename-with-references is one command (Requirement 11.4).
- **`DatabricksContextPropertyProvider`** — the Requirement 10 grids, including the read-only `Workspace connection` placeholder on every file level and the simulated-last-run read-only property.
- **`DatabricksToolboxProvider`** — per-type entries (task types; notebook/file library; job/pipeline resource skeletons), dropped via placement ids.
- **`DatabricksValidator`** — Requirement 12's findings with file and line, registered into the problems pipeline.

### Client: canvases

- **`BundleCanvas`, `JobCanvas`, `PipelineCanvas`** — three components registered for the three MIME types, all composed from the central canvas library; module CSS carries the family's classes. The job canvas reuses the timeline's interaction set: drag to reposition (dispatching the layout command rather than a model move), anchor-drag relations via `rel:` ids, toolbox drops via `new:` ids, the shared context-menu hook.
- **Simulation engine (client-only)** — a small `useSimulatedRun` hook: given the parsed DAG and a mock profile, it plays pending → running → succeeded/failed transitions over time and feeds per-element badge state to the canvas. The canvas's own menu/ribbon callback intercepts the simulated action ids before calling `executeAction`, starts the local show, and still reports the execution so menus stay backend-driven. This keeps simulations out of the history by construction (Requirement 11.6) and needs no core change — the established workaround for the context channel carrying no gesture data.

## Data Models

Wire payloads in `src/diagrams/databricks/api/databricks.proto` (one message per element kind, carried as `Any` on the shared `Element`):

```proto
message DatabricksTaskPayload {
  string task_key = 1;
  string task_type = 2;          // notebook, python, wheel, sql, dbt, pipeline, run-job, condition, for-each, jar, other
  string source = 3;             // the type's principal source field, display form
  string cluster_key = 4;        // empty = serverless
  string run_if = 5;             // empty = ALL_SUCCESS
  bool unresolved = 6;           // a depends_on stub target (R4.5)
}
message DatabricksEdgePayload { string outcome = 1; }   // "", "true", "false"
message DatabricksResourcePayload { string kind = 1; string key = 2; string defining_file = 3; }
message DatabricksTargetPayload { string mode = 1; bool is_default = 2; int32 override_count = 3; }
message DatabricksPipelineNodePayload { string role = 1; /* source|pipeline|target|compute|notifications */ string label = 2; repeated string badges = 3; }
```

The `.adp` grows two headers beside `body:`/`view:`: `resource:` (which key in a multi-resource file) and the `layout:` block (core-owned, described above).

## Error Handling

### Error Scenarios

1. **Body does not parse** — the diagram opens unavailable naming the parse error; every provider refuses edits with the same reason (Requirement 2.3).
2. **Schema-invalid edit** (duplicate task key, rename to an existing key, removing a library the schema requires) — refused by the writer before any splice; the dialog or property grid shows the writer's sentence.
3. **`depends_on` to a missing task** — rendered as a stub edge to a marked missing node; validation names it (Requirement 4.5); connect/disconnect still work on the healthy parts.
4. **Cycles** — layout excludes back-edges from layering but draws them; validation names the cycle members (Requirement 4.6); no crash, no hang.
5. **Stale layout ids in the `.adp`** — ignored on read, dropped on next write; a config that gained elements places them by computed layout (Requirement 7.4/7.5).
6. **Simulated action invoked with no visible canvas effect possible** (e.g. from the ribbon while loading) — the action completes as a no-op; the marker property still says simulation, and nothing lands on the history.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Testing

- Parser/writer per format: parse fixtures, byte-identity on the untouched round trip, smallest-diff splices for every named operation, refusals for schema-invalid writes. Fixture `.yml`/`.json` files whose bytes are the test subject get a narrowly-scoped `Fixtures/**` `-text` line in `.gitattributes` limited to this module's fixture files by full glob — the by-extension rule cannot apply to extensions the whole repository shares, and the glob is written tight enough to catch only the fixtures, with the reasoning recorded beside the existing `.gitattributes` commentary.
- Layout functions on fixture DAGs, including the cycle and missing-target cases.
- `RegistrationLayout` (core tests): read/merge/stale-drop/write, and `SetRegistrationLayoutCommand` undo restoring the prior entry byte-for-byte in the `.adp`.
- Providers: discovery per selection kind, every command's execute/undo/redo, rename-with-references, the simulated ids discovering with markers and executing without dispatch.
- Client: canvas tests per type over mocked streams (structure, badges, stub edges), the `useSimulatedRun` hook's state machine, menu interception of simulated ids.

### Integration Testing

- The gRPC flow per type: open, edit, undo against the real host, deltas observed.
- `ExampleRegistrationTests` extended by construction: the Requirement 13 examples resolve, open and validate clean (Requirement 13.5) in the existing sweep.
- Layout persistence end-to-end: move an element, reopen the diagram, position survives; undo returns it; the body file's bytes unchanged throughout.

### End-to-End Testing

- A `tests.md` entry per family behavior that only a running app shows: the simulated job run's ripple honoring `run_if`/`outcome`, the simulated deploy's progress over a target's resources, and the reposition-then-reopen layout check — each with preconditions, actions and expected results, runnable as a manual verification pass.
